newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan shilling slips versus dollar on oil demand.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan shilling slips versus dollar on oil demand.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling edged lower on the dollar and pound on increased demand for hard currency by oil companies, commercial bank dealers said.
"There is consistent pressure on the shilling right now, which has forced it a little lower. You could say it is barely stable. There is plenty of commercial pressure," a dealer said.

"At least two oil companies wanted dollars in the range of up to $10 million. There is this one (company) whose obligations may be up to $50 million. Now, ours (Kenya) is a small market and when orders come big like that, shilling weakness is expected," the dealer added.
"In the near-term, the shilling may be maintained at a position considered stable but weak," the dealer said.

The Central Bank of Kenya posted the shilling at a commercial rate of 56.99 against the dollar compared to 56.93 on Monday. It quoted a commercial mean of 88.95 against the pound versus 88.86 on Monday.
Central Bank of Kenya means are compiled from the quoted rates of the 10 leading commercial banks in Kenya.
On Monday, inter-bank trading was dull with some sporadic dollar buying as traders continued covering positions internally.
"A number of traders were back quoting two way prices, but the spreads remained at 20 cents," a commercial dealer said.
